sources.handbook: Cornell Engineering Undergraduate Handbook Fall 2025, EP pp. 76-79 (notes c, e, f, g, h)

pageRules: e. Students are required to take two out of the following three courses: AEP 3560, AEP 3620, AEP 4340. If all three are taken, the third can be counted as a Major-approved Elective. Students who plan to pursue Ph.D. degrees in physics are advised to take AEP 3560 and AEP 3620.

h. Six Major-approved Electives: (1) All Major-approved Electives must be technical electives. (2) Five of the six courses must be at or above the 3000-level. (3) Nine credits of Major-approved Electives must be outside of AEP. (4) Only three independent study/research courses may be taken as Major-approved Electives and must be taken during the last four semesters. (5) If a third AEP course from note 'e' above is taken, it may be counted as a required Major-approved Elective. (6) All Major-approved Electives must be taken for a letter grade (C- or better).
Department page: 'Two of the following are required.' AEP 3560, AEP 3620, AEP 4340.

Catalog: Major-Approved Elective (any level): Must be technical courses taken for a letter grade (3-4). Major Approved Upper Level Elective (3000 level or above): All must be technical courses taken for a letter grade (15-20). Minimum of 18 credit required for major-approved electives.
c. AEP 3330 may simultaneously satisfy major and distribution requirements. In this case, the total number of credits required for the degree is a minimum of 133.

technical.why: Note h(1): all must be technical electives. Engineering, math and science subjects (the subject sets earlier sweep builders use for 'technical'), 3+ credits (the seat's minimum). Research and independent study stay in: up to three count (note h(4)).
technical.exceptWhy: College rule (handbook p.23): nothing below 1100 counts, nor pre-curriculum courses 'such as CS 1109 or MATH 1110'; the Fall 2026 handbook also names MATH 1900.
